# WO-2026-08-09-08 — Restore rule 37

## This corrects LARRY'S error, not the previous worker's

`WO-B15-R3` archived rule 37 on **my** reading. Warwick has overruled it, and he is right. His words:

> *"DO NOT ARCHIVE RULE 37. I am explicitly retaining the Sure rule. **You have conflated two
> different classes of behaviour:**
>
> **1. PRICE/VALUE JUDGEMENT — archive this.** … anything that requires current price/offer
> arithmetic to choose the economically 'best' option.
>
> **2. DETERMINABLE HOUSEHOLD SHOPPING POLICY — retain this. Rule 37 is in this class.**
>
> The Sure rule is determinable before the browser run. … **Do not discard a deterministic
> quantity/variant rule merely because its prose mentions a multibuy context.** The product decision
> I made was: ARCHIVE THE BEST-VALUE / BARGAIN-SHOPPING JUDGEMENT. It was NOT: ARCHIVE EVERY RULE
> THAT MENTIONS AN OFFER OR MULTIBUY."*

**The live rule text is the whole argument, and it settles it:** rule 37 states its own outcome
arithmetically and price-free — **`Mum 3 male -> add 1 female = 4`**. Rounding 3 up to 4 and adding
one female variant needs **no price, no offer state, no browser**. The `any 2 for £X` clause is *why
the household adopted the habit*, not an input the planner evaluates.

**The distinction you must hold throughout:** *does the outcome require price arithmetic?* — not
*does the prose mention an offer?*

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Rule 37's behaviour is executable in planning again.** A Sure line asking for an **odd**
  quantity is rounded **UP to the next even number**, and the **female variant is added to complete
  the final pair**. Resolved **before** the browser handoff, from grounded catalogue and household
  data already available. The live example is the canonical case: **3 male → add 1 female → 4**.
- **AC2 — It works with NO price data whatsoever.** Drive AC1 from a catalogue carrying **no price
  field at all** (`UNPRICED_PODS` in `rulebook.test.js` is the existing shape for this). **If your
  implementation needs a price to produce the answer, you have built the wrong thing.**
- **AC3 — Its regression coverage is restored**, per Warwick's *"keep its regression coverage"*. R3
  re-cut rule 37's case away; it comes back. **Do not delete the non-price cases R3 added in its
  place** — the rulebook's other job is still real, so the suite should grow, not swap.
- **AC4 — R3's archival control SURVIVES and still fires.** The control that fails if price
  arithmetic re-enters must remain, and must **not** be weakened to accommodate rule 37 — rule 37
  needs no price, so a correct implementation does not strain it. **Mutation-test it again in both
  directions** and show it still goes RED. **If restoring rule 37 forces you to relax that control,
  STOP and report it** — that would mean the implementation is using price.
- **AC5 — Only rules 31 and 36 remain archived.** Established by live query, staged at
  `Deliverables/2026-08-09-live-rule-corpus-and-value-rule-identification.md`. Assert against your
  own diff that nothing else was removed, and that the Nescafe rules (12/25 — `needs_decision`,
  which **asks** rather than optimises) are untouched.
- **AC6 — The two stale documents are corrected.** `skill/README.md` still says *"Nothing is wired.
  No pipeline caller invokes `applyRulebook` yet."* — **R2 made that false.**
  `pipeline/rulebookWiring.test.js:8` says the rulebook has *"29 of its own tests"* and its fixture
  rule texts are still worded as best-value / pair-rounding rules. Make both true.
- **AC7 — Counts, all eight suites, before and after.** Assert the count, never the exit code. `skill`
  must still show exactly its **7** pre-existing environment failures and no eighth.

## Required evidence

- All eight suites executed with **counts** before and after: `pipeline`, `handoff`, `packet`,
  `browser-runner`, `bot`, `intake`, `reconcile`, `skill`.
- **The AC1/AC2 case executed and pasted** — the odd-quantity Sure line going in, the even quantity
